text: ConversationConfig::Builder defaults in LiteRT-LM agello-next (runtime/conversation/conversation.h): enable_constrained_decoding false, prefill_preface_on_init false, filter_channel_content_from_kv_cache true, return_error_on_parse_failure true, return_error_on_max_tokens_reached false, stream_tool_calls false with channel name "tool_call", enable_rewinding true; ConversationConfig::CreateDefault(engine) is Builder().Build(engine).

ConversationConfig::CreateInternal copies the SessionConfig, sets ApplyPromptTemplateInSession(false) on the copy and validates it against the engine settings (MaybeUpdateAndValidate), so the Session never applies its own prompt templates for a Conversation.

ConversationConfig::CreateInternal picks the prompt template in this order: the overwrite template; the model metadata's jinja_prompt_template; a default Jinja template generated from metadata prompt_templates and llm_model_type (GetDefaultJinjaPromptTemplate); otherwise it fails with InvalidArgument.

ConversationConfig::CreateInternal takes channels from the overwrite list if given, else from LlmMetadata.channels (name, start, end, is_reasoning_channel), and rejects any channel with an empty channel_name.

Without an overwrite, the data processor config comes from CreateDataProcessorConfigFromLlmModelType on the SessionConfig's llm_model_type, which maps kGemma4 to CreateGemma4DataProcessorConfig and returns InvalidArgument for unsupported model types.
litert::lm::Message is an nlohmann::ordered_json; Preface is std::variant<JsonPreface> with fields messages, tools and extra_context; Channel has channel_name, start, end and is_reasoning_channel.

NormalizeMessageContent turns a string content into [{"type":"text","text":...}], wraps an object content in a one-element array, keeps arrays, and leaves messages without content (e.g. assistant tool calls) unchanged; it is the default ModelDataProcessor::MessageToTemplateInput.

LoadItemData loads an image or audio content item from "path" (memory-mapped file) or "blob" (base64, decoded into memory), fails if neither is present, returns nothing for text-less "tool_response" items, and rejects other item types as Unimplemented.

OptionalArgs (conversation.h) carries per-message settings: has_pending_message, repetition_penalty_config, no_repeat_ngram_config, suppress_tokens_config, decoding_constraint, data processor args, max_output_tokens (thinking and answer tokens both count), task_group_id, extra_context (merged over the preface's) and thinking_config (overrides the ConversationConfig's).

ThinkingConfig's default constructor means thinking enabled with thinking_token_budget -1 (unlimited); ResolveThinkingConfig uses OptionalArgs.thinking_config when set, else the ConversationConfig's, else none.

PromptTemplate (runtime/components/prompt_template.cc) renders with minijinja through a Rust FFI; its capabilities have one field, supports_single_turn, which is true exactly when the template source contains the string "is_appending_to_prefill".

Before parsing, EditTemplateForMinijinja rewrites Python string idioms in the template with regexes (.startswith/.endswith to tests, .replace/.split/.join/.lstrip/.rstrip/.strip/.items to filters) and deletes {% generation %} and {% endgeneration %}.

The minijinja environment keeps trailing newlines and enables trim_blocks and lstrip_blocks; it adds the functions strftime_now and raise_exception, the filters tojson, lstrip and rstrip, and the test none.

MinijinjaTemplate::apply_impl builds a new minijinja Environment and re-adds (re-parses) the template source on every render, and copies each extra_context key to the top level of the template context (so extra_context {"enable_thinking": true} is visible to the template as enable_thinking).

PromptTemplateInput.bos_token defaults to an empty string, so a template's {{ bos_token }} renders nothing in Conversation; the BOS token (the SessionConfig start token) is instead prepended by ApplyPromptTemplates on the first prefill of a fresh session when session-level templating is off.
Conversation::ApplyTemplate removes the "blob" field of image and audio items (StripBlobsFromTemplateInput) before rendering, so base64 media never enters the template.

The Gemma 4 E2B and E4B .litertlm files (Agello's e4b-ours, Google's E4B at 2eee7ac3 and E2B at b3ca0d2f) carry the same jinja_prompt_template, start token id 2, stop tokens 1, 50 and 106, and one channel named "thought" with start "<|channel>thought\n" and end "<channel|>" (is_reasoning_channel not set).

text: The template in the Gemma 4 E2B/E4B .litertlm files does not contain "is_appending_to_prefill", so PromptTemplate reports supports_single_turn=false and Conversation renders each turn with GetSingleTurnTextFromFullHistory (two full renders and a string difference).

Conversation::GetSingleTurnText rejects OptionalArgs.has_pending_message=true with InvalidArgument when the template doesn't support single-turn rendering, which is the case for the Gemma 4 E2B/E4B file templates.

For the first message of a Conversation (history empty, prefill_preface_on_init false) the prefill text is the full render of the preface messages, tools and extra context plus the new message(s) with add_generation_prompt=true.

For later messages, Conversation::GetSingleTurnTextFromFullHistory renders preface plus history with add_generation_prompt=false (old) and preface plus history plus the new message(s) with add_generation_prompt=true (new), returns new minus its old prefix as the prefill text, and fails with InternalError if new does not start with old; only that difference is prefilled, the earlier turns stay in the KV cache.

The LiteRT-LM C API (litert_lm_conversation_create) puts the system message and the messages given with litert_lm_conversation_config_set_messages into JsonPreface.messages, not into the Conversation's history; together with the first-turn rule, a conversation created with prior messages prefills all of them, rendered in full, with its first message.

Conversation's history_ holds only the messages passed to SendMessage/SendMessageAsync (each element of an array message separately) and the completed replies; preface messages are not in GetHistory().

GetSingleTurnTextFromFullHistory sets extra_context enable_thinking from the resolved ThinkingConfig and merges OptionalArgs.extra_context over the preface's extra context (existing keys overwritten) before rendering.

The Gemma 4 E2B/E4B file template opens a system turn ('<|turn>system
') when enable_thinking is true, tools are present or the first message is system/developer, emits '<|think|>' at its top when enable_thinking is true, renders role assistant as 'model', ends each non-tool turn with '<turn|>
', and adds '<|turn>model
' as generation prompt unless the last message was a tool response.

sources.detail: jinja_prompt_template: system block, message loop, add_generation_prompt block

text: The Gemma 4 E2B/E4B file template passes assistant ('model') text through a strip_thinking macro that drops every '<|channel>...<channel|>' span and trims the result, so prior reasoning is never rendered into the prompt.

sources.detail: jinja_prompt_template: macro strip_thinking and its use for role model

text: The jinja_prompt_template in the Gemma 4 E2B/E4B .litertlm files differs from chat_template.jinja in google/gemma-4-E4B-it at revision ee0ef602 (headed 'Google Gemma 4 Canonical Chat Template', published 2026-07-09, 'Fixed tool-calling loops, turn closures, and thinking content-ordering'); for example the Hugging Face template emits '<|think|>\n' where the file template emits '<|think|>', and only the Hugging Face template renders reasoning_content and resolves tool responses by tool_call_id.

sources.detail: jinja_prompt_template ('<|think|>' without a newline; no reasoning_content handling)

text: The Gemma 4 -gpu .litertlm files carry a different template from the standard E2B/E4B files: after a tool response with enable_thinking it adds '<|channel>thought\n' as the generation prompt.

text: ModelDataProcessor's interface is ToInputDataVector (rendered prompt plus messages to InputData), ToMessage (responses to a Message), MessageToTemplateInput (default NormalizeMessageContent), FormatTools (default identity), CreateConstraint (default Unimplemented), CodeFenceStart/End (default empty) and CloneState.

ModelDataProcessorRegistry maps each DataProcessorConfig variant index to a creator; EnsureBuiltinProcessorsRegistered registers Generic always and Gemma 3, Gemma 4, FunctionGemma, Qwen3, FastVLM, MiniCPM5, MiniCPM-V and LFM2 only under their ENABLE_*_DATA_PROCESSOR defines; an unregistered family yields Unimplemented.

Gemma4DataProcessorConfig defaults: boi "<|image>", eoi "<image|>", boa "<|audio>", eoa "<audio|>", 16x16 patches, max_num_patches 2520, pooling_kernel_size 3, merge_patches false, code fence "<|tool_call>"/"<tool_call|>", quotes "<|\"|>", function_response_start "<|tool_response>", syntax "fc", escape_fence_strings true, constraint mode kTextAndOr; CreateGemma4DataProcessorConfig overrides fields whose metadata value differs from the proto default.
Gemma4DataProcessor overrides neither MessageToTemplateInput nor FormatTools, so tool declarations and assistant tool_calls reach the Jinja template as JSON and the template formats them.

Gemma4DataProcessor::ToInputDataVectorImpl calls ProcessMultimodalPrompt, which splits the rendered prompt at <|image|>/<start_of_image>/<|audio|>/<start_of_audio> placeholders and replaces each image placeholder with InputText(text before + boi token), the preprocessed InputImage and InputImageEnd (audio likewise with InputAudio and InputAudioEnd), keeping the remaining text as InputText.

ProcessMultimodalPrompt sets an image's max_num_patches to visual_token_budget x pooling_kernel_size^2 when a budget is given (non-positive budgets are rejected); with Gemma 4's default pooling_kernel_size 3 and max_num_patches 2520 (also in the E2B/E4B file metadata) the default image budget is 280 tokens.
formula: max_num_patches = visual_token_budget x pooling_kernel_size^2; with the defaults (pooling 3, max_num_patches 2520) the implicit budget is 2520 / (3 x 3) = 280 tokens per image

text: Conversation::SendMessageAsync rejects a Gemma 4 visual_token_budget that is not positive or exceeds the engine's max vision tokens per image (when that engine setting is present).
ProcessMultimodalPrompt fails with InvalidArgument when the messages carry fewer or more images (or audio clips) than the rendered prompt has placeholders.

ResponseTextToMessage (used by Gemma4DataProcessor::ToMessageImpl) parses tool calls only when the preface has a non-empty tools list; otherwise the whole response text becomes one text content item of an assistant message.

Conversation::Create creates a new Engine::Session for each Conversation (engine.CreateSession with the config's SessionConfig), then the model data processor and, if a ConstraintProviderConfig is set, the constraint provider.
With prefill_preface_on_init true and a non-empty preface, Conversation::Create renders the preface alone (add_generation_prompt false) and prefills it before returning.

Template rendering and media preprocessing (ToInputDataVector) run on the thread that calls SendMessageAsync, and SessionAdvanced::RunPrefillAsync tokenizes the inputs before queuing the prefill task.

Conversation::SendMessage is SendMessageAsync plus session WaitUntilDone and a wait for the completion notification; it returns history_.back() (the reply), or an empty Message when the conversation was appending.

After a successful (or empty-input) prefill, SendMessageAsync's prefill callback schedules RunDecodeAsync with the DecodeConfig built by CreateDecodeConfig; prefill errors and non-Done end states go to the internal callback without decoding.

CreateInternalCallback streams text outside channels through ModelDataProcessor::ToMessage, streams channel text as {"role":"assistant","channels":{name:text}} (plus reasoning_content for reasoning channels), and holds back a trailing partial match of a channel start or end delimiter until the next chunk.

The internal callback treats the tool-call code fence as a channel with an empty name: it buffers the whole block including fences and emits it through ToMessage only when the end fence arrives; with stream_tool_calls the text inside the fences is also streamed on the tool-call channel.

At kDone, SendCompleteMessage flushes unsent text, extracts named-channel spans from the accumulated text (an unterminated span runs to the end), builds the final message with ToMessage, inserts the spans under "channels" (reasoning channels also under "reasoning_content"), calls complete_message_callback and then sends the empty-Message completion sentinel.
A channel is a reasoning channel when its is_reasoning_channel flag is set or its name is "thought".

When decode ends with kMaxNumTokensReached and return_error_on_max_tokens_reached is false (the Builder default), the internal callback completes the reply like kDone (history and channel filtering included); when true, it removes the turn from history and reports ResourceExhausted 'Max number of tokens reached, context window out of bounds'.

CreateDecodeConfig: when the resolved ThinkingConfig enables thinking, it sets the thinking token budget and tokenizes the first configured channel's end string (and its start string, or an empty start list if the rendered prompt already opened that channel) as thinking end/start token ids; otherwise it sets the thinking token budget to 0.
Tasks::Decode wraps the decode constraint in a ThinkingBudgetConstraint whenever the thinking token budget is non-zero (including -1) and thinking end token ids are present.

With filter_channel_content_from_kv_cache on, when the rendered prompt does not end in an open channel (the Gemma 4 E2B/E4B case), the prefill callback saves the session checkpoint "channel_content_checkpoint" right after the user-turn prefill (which includes the generation prompt) and before decode, recording checkpoint_message_index_ = history size and checkpoint_after_user_prefill_ = true; it uses SaveContext instead of SaveCheckpoint when rewinding is disabled.

When the rendered prompt ends inside an open channel (GetOpenChannelName finds a start tag without a later end tag), SendMessageAsync saves the channel-content checkpoint before prefilling the user message, so the open start tag is also removed on rewind.

In agello-next, when a completed reply contains channel content and filtering is on, complete_message_callback immediately rewinds the session to the channel-content checkpoint and prefills the reply re-rendered by the template (render of history up to the checkpoint plus the reply, minus render of history up to the checkpoint with add_generation_prompt=true); the caller's completion sentinel is withheld until that refill prefill reaches kDone.

Upstream LiteRT-LM commit 97e6dc7d (2026-10-07, 'Eagerly filter channel content from KV cache after decode') replaced the lazy pre-turn refill with the eager post-decode refill; it is part of agello-next's base df6df5b8 and not of v0.18.0.

sources.quote: Switch channel/thinking-token KV cache cleanup in `Conversation` from lazy pre-turn refill to eager post-decode refill

text: In the shipped v0.18.0 source, the channel filter is lazy: a checkpoint is saved before each user message's prefill, the reply only marks channel_content_since_last_user_message_, and the next user message rewinds to that checkpoint and refills the previous user message and the reply (re-rendered) before prefilling the new message.

SessionAdvanced::RewindToCheckpoint restores the checkpoint's step, session state and task dependencies and drops later checkpoints; the executor's SetCurrentStep only moves current_step back (and marks the MTP drafter unprimed), so a rewind copies no KV data and the refill overwrites the abandoned positions.
The LiteRT-LM C API disables Conversation rewinding (switching the channel filter to SaveContext/RestoreContext) only when the main executor's GpuArtisanConfig has use_autosized_ringbuffers set.

The Swift wrapper passes filter_channel_content_from_kv_cache to the C API only when ExperimentalFlags.filterChannelContentFromKvCache is non-nil (its default is nil); unset, the C++ Builder default (true) applies.
Agello (93122b6) sets ExperimentalFlags.filterChannelContentFromKvCache = true when it loads a model, so reasoning is removed from the KV cache in its conversations.

A per-message ThinkingConfig changes enable_thinking in both renders of GetSingleTurnTextFromFullHistory, so the prefill difference never contains the system turn: the '<|think|>' marker (or its absence) written by the first prefill stays in the KV cache for later turns of the same Conversation.

sources.detail: jinja_prompt_template system block ('<|think|>' only in the system turn)

text: Gemma 4 tool calls are parsed from the text between '<|tool_call>' and '<tool_call|>' with the FC syntax, whose ANTLR grammar (parsed in Rust) is 'call:NAME{key:value,...}' with strings delimited by '<|"|>', '<escape>' or '<ctrl46>'; each parsed call becomes {"type":"function","function":{...}} in tool_calls.

If a tool-call block fails to parse and return_error_on_parse_failure is true (the default), ParseTextAndToolCalls fails the whole reply with InvalidArgument; if false, the block is kept as a text item with an "error" field.

The tool-call parsers (FC, JSON, Python) are linked unless //build_config:disable_tool_use_parser is set, in which case parser_utils uses antlr_parser_utils_noop; the --config=agello block in .bazelrc does not set it.
The Swift Conversation's automatic tool loop runs at most 25 model calls per sendMessage (recurringToolCallLimit) and passes the per-message thinkingConfig only on the first call.

The Swift wrapper skips a responseFormat for a non-tool message when automatic tool calling is on and the conversation has tools, and applies it to tool-response messages and to conversations without tools.

ConstraintProviderConfig is std::variant<ExternalConstraintConfig, LlGuidanceConfig, FstConfig>; FstConfig has a deleted constructor (a placeholder), and CreateConstraintProvider builds only ExternalConstraintProvider or LlgConstraintProvider, returning Unimplemented for anything else.

When LlGuidanceConfig.eos_id is unset (as the C API leaves it), CreateConstraintProvider uses the first single-token stop sequence of the SessionConfig; for the Gemma 4 E2B/E4B files, whose stop tokens are 1, 50 and 106 in that order, llguidance's EOS is token 1.

LlgConstraintProvider::Create builds an llguidance tokenizer from every token of the model's vocabulary (special tokens flagged with a 0xFF prefix byte) and CreateConstraint makes a regex, JSON-schema, Lark or llguidance-internal constraint, failing with InternalError on a grammar error.

The C API maps kLiteRtLmConstraintTypeRegex and kLiteRtLmConstraintTypeJsonSchema to an LlGuidanceConstraintArg in OptionalArgs.decoding_constraint (no Lark or external constraints through C), and litert_lm_conversation_config_set_constraint_provider accepts only kLiteRtLmConstraintProviderTypeLlGuidance.

Swift ConversationConfig(enableResponseFormat: true) sets the constraint provider to LlGuidance and enables constrained decoding; otherwise enable_constrained_decoding follows ExperimentalFlags.enableConversationConstrainedDecoding (default false). ResponseFormat offers .json(schema:) and .regex(pattern:).

Conversation::CreateDecodeConfig uses OptionalArgs.decoding_constraint through the conversation's constraint provider when both exist; otherwise, if constrained decoding is enabled, no constraint exists yet and the preface has tools, it asks the model data processor for a tool-call constraint and ignores an Unimplemented answer.

Conversation keeps the constraint it creates in the member constraint_ and never clears it; CreateDecodeConfig passes constraint_ to every later decode, so a response-format constraint given with one message also constrains later messages of the same Conversation that pass none.

Our Apple builds use --config=agello (agello/build-xcframework.sh), which defines LITERT_LM_FST_CONSTRAINTS_DISABLED=1 (ours: 43f0f5c3); that selects //build_config:disable_fst_constraints, so the Gemma 3, Gemma 4 and FunctionGemma processors are compiled with LITERT_LM_FST_CONSTRAINTS_DISABLED and without gemma_model_constraint_provider_lib.

With LITERT_LM_FST_CONSTRAINTS_DISABLED, Gemma4DataProcessor::Create succeeds even when constrained decoding is requested and Gemma4DataProcessor::CreateConstraint returns Unimplemented ('Tool-call constraints need the FST constraint provider...'), which Conversation skips (ours: d1488ce7, same change for Gemma 3 and FunctionGemma).

In the v0.18.0 source (and upstream before our d1488ce7), building with LITERT_LM_FST_CONSTRAINTS_DISABLED made Gemma4DataProcessor::Create fail with FailedPrecondition ('Constrained decoding was disabled at build time.') whenever constrained decoding was enabled, which blocked llguidance response formats too.

text: The Gemma model constraint provider (FST, closed source) is a prebuilt libGemmaModelConstraintProvider.dylib for ios_arm64, ios_sim_arm64 and macos_arm64 (and .so/.dll elsewhere), linked through gemma_model_constraint_provider_shared_lib.
generated/binaries.md: Google's prebuilt v0.18.0 CLiteRTLM (iOS arm64) defines 17 Gemma-constraint-provider/FST symbols and ours defines none; both define llguidance symbols (127 and 92).

text: In the v0.18.0 source with the FST provider compiled in, Gemma4DataProcessor::Create with constrained decoding enabled creates the closed provider from the serialized SentencePiece model and the stop-token sequences (only for a SentencePiece tokenizer; otherwise it logs a warning and continues without one).

A JSON response format sent from the Swift wrapper takes the llguidance path in both agello-next and the shipped v0.18.0 wrapper: enableResponseFormat sets the LlGuidance provider, the C API turns the format into an LlGuidanceConstraintArg, and CreateDecodeConfig builds the constraint through that provider; the FST provider is only consulted for tool-call constraints built from the preface's tools.
Agello (93122b6) runs each JSON helper prompt on a new Conversation created with enableResponseFormat true and speculative decoding off, and its chat conversations don't enable constrained decoding.
ExternalConstraintConfig lets a C++ caller pass its own Constraint object (ExternalConstraintArg) per message; the C API has no way to pass one.

On cancellation, Conversation's cancel_callback pops the messages the cancelled send added to history and clears the channel checkpoint, but does not rewind the session: the cancelled turn's prefilled and decoded tokens stay in the KV cache.

Conversation::CancelProcess calls SessionAdvanced::CancelProcess, which cancels all tasks of the session; both headers say reusing the conversation or session afterwards is neither recommended nor supported (the session is left poisoned).
Conversation::CancelGroup cancels only tasks registered under an OptionalArgs.task_group_id, and the C API's CreateOptionalArgs never sets task_group_id.

Conversation::GetTokenCount returns the session's current step (tokens in the KV cache from prefill and decode); CountTokens renders a prospective message against the current history and counts its tokens, media included, without changing the conversation.

Conversation::Clone clones the session, creates a new model data processor (copying its state) and constraint provider, and copies history and the appending flag; the member constraint_ and the channel checkpoint index are not copied.
Conversation::RunTextScoring scores target text on a clone of the session, leaving the conversation's history and KV state unchanged.

SessionAdvanced::SaveCheckpoint records only the current step, session state and last task ids under a label; SaveContext additionally stores a ProcessedContext from the execution manager, which RestoreContext gives back.
